answer: A farm can script one good paragraph per identity, but it cannot improvise a hundred defences at once. After each answer, pair the identity with a random stranger who asks two follow-ups drawn from its own claims: why this step, what breaks it. Grade the replies for consistency and specific detail. Copied identities give the same defence, contradict their own text, or wander from the question. A wharf holds only ships that actually dock; a cedar is known by its grain under close inspection, not its silhouette. Make questioning the dock.
